doc.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018

title: Whether things are better: wealth data and media
summary: He cites racial wealth data and people ignoring facts.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Wow. Thanks for sharing that. What do you say when someone says, “Yeah but things are much better than they used to be”?

Well for some and everything. But you know if you look at the data of fallen African- American men and women, through no fault, they haven’t done anything. I mean I think the numbers are still pretty high and everything and all. So the thing is, things can be seen as better because we have Oprah Winfrey and these other people that have done very well for themselves and everything. But there was a very interesting report, I don’t know if you saw that, coming out of Boston, that says like the average white family in Boston has assets of about 240, around the two hundred thousand range and everything. And the African-American and Hispanic, theirs is zero to below zero of money in relationship to debt and income you know. So the amount of money that they have coming in to cover their expenses just covers their expenses. Sometimes it may not. So if you look at their total resources in relationship to debt and income, you know, they are in the minus column you know, or at zero. So when you look at those numbers you say well things are better for some and things are, even though they seem to be better for others are not really that much better. But a lot of people don’t look at data. They just turn on the television and turn to their favorite station and have that poor person just pour on all the information of what they want to hear. They don’t want to hear the other things. I mean it’s evident. Because if you talk to someone about the president, you say well the president is, well he’s done X, he’s done Y, he’s done Z, he’s done that you know. We don’t care. We don’t care what he’s done. We don’t care. I mean even women. Women say we don’t care he’s a this and we don’t care he’s a that, we just don’t care. So I mean what do you do in that type of circumstance, when you present information and data to a person, and facts and everything, and they say they don’t care. I mean just like the whole thing about
Obama being born in Kenya. I mean the data is there to say that, but then they say that almost 30% of the population still thinks that he was born in Kenya and he’s a Muslim.
